name: Tick

features.claim: An adult tick is about 3 to 5 mm long.
features.quote: Adult ticks are approximately 3 to 5 mm in length depending on age, sex, and species, but can become larger when engorged.

features.claim: A tick's body is ovoid or pear-shaped.
features.quote: Adults have ovoid/pear-shaped bodies (idiosomas) which become engorged with blood when they feed, and eight legs.
Adults have ovoid/pear-shaped bodies (idiosomas) which become engorged with blood when they feed, and eight legs.

features.claim: A tick's body swells up with blood when it feeds.
features.quote: Adults have ovoid/pear-shaped bodies (idiosomas) which become engorged with blood when they feed, and eight legs.

features.claim: A tick's head-part and body are completely joined together.
features.quote: Their cephalothorax and abdomen are completely fused.

features.claim: A hard tick has a hard shield on its back called a scutum.
features.quote: In addition to having a hard shield on their dorsal surfaces, known as the scutum, hard ticks have a beak-like structure at the front containing the mouthparts, whereas soft ticks have their mouthparts on the underside of their bodies.

features.claim: A hard tick has a beak-like part at the front holding its mouthparts.
features.quote: In addition to having a hard shield on their dorsal surfaces, known as the scutum, hard ticks have a beak-like structure at the front containing the mouthparts, whereas soft ticks have their mouthparts on the underside of their bodies.

features.claim: A soft tick's mouthparts are on the underside of its body, so you cannot see them from above.
features.quote: The mouthparts cannot be seen from above, as they are on the ventral surface.

features.claim: Most ticks are plain brown or reddish brown.
features.quote: Most ticks are plain brown or reddish brown.

features.claim: A tick's legs have seven segments and end in a pair of claws.
features.quote: In the nymphal and adult stages, ticks have eight legs, each of which has seven segments and is tipped with a pair of claws.

features.claim: A tick's legs often have sensory or tactile hairs on them.
features.quote: The legs are sometimes ornamented and usually bear sensory or tactile hairs.

features.claim: When a tick is not moving, its legs stay folded tightly against its body.
features.quote: When stationary, their legs remain tightly folded against the body.

second_reading.quote: A common misconception about ticks is they jump onto their host: They are incapable of jumping, although static electricity from their hosts has been shown to be capable of pulling the tick over distances several times their own body length.

second_reading.claim: When ticks first appeared is not certain.
second_reading.quote: The timing of the origin of ticks is uncertain, though the oldest known tick fossils are around 100 million years old, and come from the Cretaceous period.
